newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan mulls more fuel-efficient engines.
newsitem.headline: Nissan mulls more fuel-efficient engines.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it is considering installing direct-injection gasoline engines in its cars.
A Nissan spokesman, however, denied a newspaper report that it plans to start launching models equipped with the fuel-efficient engines, still relatively new to the industry, this autumn.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily reported in its evening edition on Wednesday that Nissan plans to spend two to three billion yen at its Iwaki plant in northern Japan to produce a luxury sedan equipped with direct-injection engines.
The company plans to be making 2,000 of the engines per month by the end of 1998, the paper said.
Mitsubishi Motors Corp was the world's first automaker to use the engines in its models. The company launched its first model equipped with the new engines in August 1996.
Toyota Motor Corp also began using the engines in December 1996.
